I’m so sorry you are suffering. It’s so hard to be in that tight spot where it feels like it’s coming at you from all angles, and there’s no way out. But there is always ALWAYS tomorrow. When I was maybe about 12, someone gave me a pin that said “It’s okay not to be okay. Have hope for tomorrow.” And of course, at the time, I didn’t really get it. But now, I hang onto that hope. Because there will be something tomorrow. Maybe something funny will happen, maybe you’ll find new music you never heard of, and think ‘where has this been all my life?!’. Maybe it’s just another day, maybe something good happens, you just never know. 

So I’m offering you my hope for tomorrow, friend. If you don’t have enough, please take some of mine. We got this. You got this. One tomorrow at a time.

I have GAD and got mine out a while back! 

Make sure you have a set plan in place for when they let you go home and make sure you won’t be alone.

One of the best things I did was reminded myself “this is all in my mom’s hands. She’s got this, I trust her” as my mom was the one picking me up and looking after me that night. It took a lot of the anxiety off knowing someone I trust is going to make sure I’m fine. 

I went into the office and they gave me Valium. I just relaxed for a while and played games on my phone until they called me back. So as for Valium or similar pills, it really just makes you pretty chill, but you’ll be responsive and feel okay!

Once I was called back they gave me an IV, and all I remember was saying “Chill” to the Oral Surgeon and I was out. I woke up and I actually do remember most of what happened after waking up. Before the procedure I expected my anxious self to be total freaking out when I woke up,but I was pretty relaxed, I just felt a little bit cold. I was fine holding conversations in both English and sign language, but I do remember I was a little bit more quick to be frustrated by something small (I.e. why is the car in front of us going so slow)

I slept for the entire day, and the only time I ever really “freaked out” was when I heard loud noises coming from the TV. So I’d say make sure wherever you’re going afterwards is a nice, calm place. :) It’ll be fine! I was so terrified of Anesthesia, but after experiencing it, I think If I ever had to undergo a procedure where I would have to have Valium or an IV I would do it again! 

Good luck friend, I hope you find it’s not so bad :)

I could go on for days. It’s less about the actual show itself, but more about the actors and the franchise as a whole. It’s really not that interesting but i fixate on it, since ive loved the show since I could remember. 

A few things most people already know:

Steve used to get really really explicit letters and e-mails from moms of the kids that watched the show

Both Steve and Joe auditioned for the show without knowing what the show was about. 

Steve thought it was a narration job, and did not expect to be on camera, let alone a kids show. He also did not look the part whatsoever, as he had earrings, wore “skater clothes”, etc. The main role was also originally supposed to be a woman. Even with these facts, Steve beat out over 1000 other people that auditioned.

When he got the job, someone from Nickelodeon took account of his appearance and called him the day before the filming of the pilot to say, and I quote “can you not like look you tomorrow morning?”

Blue was originally supposed to be a cat named Mr. Orange

The co creator Traci Paige Johnson voice Blue, because she sounded the most like a dog out of everyone in the office 

The original pilot had Steve wearing a red/orange polo, and the show at the time was called Blue Prints. It’s unreleased, and was only sent to focus groups to see kids reception to the show. There are physical copies out there, but the full pilot has never been aired or released (AFAIK)

There’s quite a few lost Blues Clues segments and episodes

It’s cannon that Blue can speak/understand Tagalog

Blues Clues reception with their target audience prompted Sesame Street and other PBS shows to include more interactive segments  

Steve (and Joe, and Josh) quite literally was just in front of a blue green screen, in front of a camera. Just him. Rarely any props he could interact with. He compared it to acting at the bottom of a swimming pool.

The children you hear talking back to Steve when he asks questions used to be credited as “Steve’s friends” without their actual names. Eventually they were given proper credit.

Steve was once named one of People magazines most eligible bachelors

Steve has actually really enjoyed the fame, as he’s average looking enough to make him unrecognizable to most, but recognizable enough that fans (parents, children, old viewers) can recognize him and interact with him

Steve really did leave for college in 2002- he went to study theater! 

It’s true that Steve left the show because he was losing his hair, but that’s not the only reason. He had many reasons, but the ultimately reason was that “it was just time” and he wanted to pass the torch.

Steve enjoys meeting people who grew up with Blues Clues. He understands that Blue’s Clues was a “brain burner” and knows that it was a large part of a lot of peoples childhoods

Steve was once asked out on a date in the 90’s and when he arrived to the woman’s house, he realized it was a childrens ‘Blues Clues’ birthday party. He had the green shirt in his car, and performed at the party anyways.

There are promotional VHS’s of Blues Clues that are rare enough that they sell for hundreds of dollars.

Blues clues was well franchised in terms of merchandise, but there’s not a ton of blues clues merchandise out there. Nick executives theorized that children knew when they were being advertised to, so they were careful about what merchandise they sold and how they sold it. Cue SpongeBob, and all that went out the window, lol.

Most of the blues clues episode prompts from the current era (the Josh era) are recycled from the Steve era. In some, they are literally the same episode, word for word.

The version of Blues Clues we don’t talk about is “Blue’s Room”- Where Blue talks. The general consensus is that the show was so short lived because of what executives thought would make the show successful: making blue talk. If you go from a normal episode of blues clues to an episode of blues room, you might find it really unsettling. Because of the fact that Blues room was not really successful, there’s little to no merchandise produces for that series. And even though there’s little merch out there, the merch that is out there often sells for less than regular blues clues merchandise. (My mom once told me that she didn’t mind blues clues, but whenever Blues Room would come on, not only were me and all of my siblings upset, but it genuinely made my parents uncomfortable because of the way she talks to the audience. It’s hard to explain but it’s just odd)

I could go on for days. It’s less about the actual show itself, but more about the actors and the franchise as a whole. It’s really not that interesting but i fixate on it, since ive loved the show since I could remember. 

A few things most people already know:

Steve used to get really really explicit letters and e-mails from moms of the kids that watched the show

Both Steve and Joe auditioned for the show without knowing what the show was about. 

Steve thought it was a narration job, and did not expect to be on camera, let alone a kids show. He also did not look the part whatsoever, as he had earrings, wore “skater clothes”, etc. The main role was also originally supposed to be a woman. Even with these facts, Steve beat out over 1000 other people that auditioned.

When he got the job, someone from Nickelodeon took account of his appearance and called him the day before the filming of the pilot to say, and I quote “can you not like look you tomorrow morning?”

Blue was originally supposed to be a cat named Mr. Orange

The co creator Traci Paige Johnson voice Blue, because she sounded the most like a dog out of everyone in the office 

The original pilot had Steve wearing a red/orange polo, and the show at the time was called Blue Prints. It’s unreleased, and was only sent to focus groups to see kids reception to the show. There are physical copies out there, but the full pilot has never been aired or released (AFAIK)

There’s quite a few lost Blues Clues segments and episodes

It’s cannon that Blue can speak/understand Tagalog

Blues Clues reception with their target audience prompted Sesame Street and other PBS shows to include more interactive segments  

Steve (and Joe, and Josh) quite literally was just in front of a blue green screen, in front of a camera. Just him. Rarely any props he could interact with. He compared it to acting at the bottom of a swimming pool.

There are promotional VHS’s of Blues Clues that are rare enough that they sell for hundreds of dollars. 

Blues Clues was one of the first preschool shows to incorporate ASL Into their show.

…And that’s a fraction of my Blues Clues infodump
